title: Spin-orbit-entangled frustrated magnetism in fcc Ba$_2$(Yb,Nd)NbO$_6$ double perovskites
authors: S. M. Hossain, Sk. Soyeb Ali, S. Mohanty, R. Kolay, M. P. Saravanan, A. K. Yogi, Y. Tokiwa, R. Nath, S. K. Panda, M. Majumder
abstract: The search for candidate Kitaev materials has largely focused on 4$d$ and 5$d$ transition-metal compounds with various lattice geometries. In contrast, investigations of rare-earth 4$f$ systems have thus far been restricted mainly to honeycomb and triangular lattices. In this work, we investigate the rare-earth-based double perovskites Ba$_2$YbNbO$_6$ and Ba$_2$NdNbO$_6$, which crystallize in a face-centered cubic structure. Magnetization and heat-capacity measurements establish isolated ${j_{\rm eff}} = 1/2$ Kramers doublet ground states arising from strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and crystal electric-field effects, which are further supported by density-functional theory calculations. Millikelvin-temperature thermodynamic measurements reveal long-range magnetic order with moderate frustration in both compounds. The emergence of magnetic order may be understood within an order-by-disorder scenario, as theoretically proposed for rare-earth fcc lattices with finite Kitaev interactions. Our results thus identify Ba$_2$YbNbO$_6$ and Ba$_2$NdNbO$_6$ as promising rare-earth spin-orbit-entangled magnets and motivate further experimental and theoretical investigations aimed at determining the complete exchange tensor to elucidate the microscopic origin of the underlying magnetic interactions.
summary: The authors investigate $	ext{Ba}_2(	ext{Yb},	ext{Nd})	ext{NbO}_6$, rare-earth double perovskites, as potential Kitaev magnets. They use combined DFT and experimental techniques to show that strong spin-orbit coupling stabilizes a $	ext{j}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ ground state in an fcc lattice. The findings establish these materials as promising candidates for studying frustrated magnetism driven by single-ion anisotropy.
main_problem: The research investigates spin-orbit-entangled frustrated magnetism in rare-earth double perovskites, aiming to find candidates for Kitaev physics beyond traditional 4d/5d materials.
main_result: The compounds $	ext{Ba}_2	ext{YbNbO}_6$ and $	ext{Ba}_2	ext{NdNbO}_6$ are identified as promising rare-earth spin-orbit-entangled magnets exhibiting long-range magnetic order with moderate frustration at low temperatures.
method: The study combines experimental measurements (magnetization, heat capacity) with advanced theoretical calculations using DFT+U+SOC to model the electronic structure and exchange interactions.
model_or_system: The physical system is based on rare-earth double perovskites ($	ext{Ba}_2(	ext{Yb},	ext{Nd})	ext{NbO}_6$) crystallizing in an fcc structure, where strong SOC stabilizes isolated $	ext{j}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ Kramers doublet ground states.
key_observables: Magnetization vs. Temperature/Field ($\chi(T), M(H)$), Heat Capacity ($C/T$), Crystal Electric Field (CEF) energy gaps, and calculated magnetic exchange tensors.
important_parameters: Low temperatures (millikelvin regime), $	ext{j}_{	ext{eff}}=1/2$ ground state, SOC strength, and frustration parameters related to Kitaev interactions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that strong SOC and CEF effects dominate the low-energy physics, leading to isolated Kramers doublets. DFT calculations use $	ext{GGA}+	ext{U}$ approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures showing the fcc arrangement of RE ions; PXRD patterns confirm phase purity; magnetization/heat capacity data reveal magnetic ordering signatures at very low temperatures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the structural and electronic ground state via DFT calculations, to characterizing the magnetic behavior using bulk measurements (magnetization, heat capacity), and finally interpreting these results in the context of frustrated magnetism and Kitaev physics.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from strongly correlated electron physics (Kitaev model) into the realm of $4f$ rare-earth oxides, providing a new platform to study SOC-driven quantum magnetic phenomena relevant to topological materials research.
